definitions.gloss: current affairs; current events issues; topical issues
definitions.explanation: Issues and topics being discussed in the news and public discourse at the present time. Often refers to questions about current events in tests and examinations.

examples.japanese: {時事|じじ}{問題|もんだい}に{関心|かんしん}がある。
examples.english: I am interested in current affairs.

examples.japanese: {入試|にゅうし}には{時事|じじ}{問題|もんだい}がよく{出|で}る。
examples.english: Current affairs questions often appear on entrance exams.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}んで{時事|じじ}{問題|もんだい}について{知識|ちしき}を{深|ふか}めている。
examples.english: I deepen my knowledge of current affairs by reading the newspaper every morning.

notes:
A compound of {時事|じじ} (current events) and {問題|もんだい} (problem/issue/question). Very common in educational and journalistic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時事|じじ}{問題|もんだい}に{詳|くわ}しい: well-informed about current affairs
- {時事|じじ}{問題|もんだい}を{取|と}り{上|あ}げる: to take up a current affairs topic
- {時事|じじ}{問題|もんだい}{対策|たいさく}: preparation for current events questions (on exams)
- {国際|こくさい}{時事|じじ}{問題|もんだい}: international current affairs issues

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {時事|じじ}: current events — the base component; refers to news events themselves
- ニュース: news — more general; refers to news reports themselves rather than analytical issues
- {社会|しゃかい}{問題|もんだい}: social issues — focuses on societal problems rather than current events broadly

USAGE:
Frequently encountered in school and exam preparation contexts, where students study {時事|じじ}{問題|もんだい} to prepare for questions about recent events on entrance exams and employment tests.
